About the Role:

As a Palliative Care Consultant, you will provide specialist medical leadership and high-quality clinical care to patients receiving palliative care services across the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN). Based within the Aged Care, Rehabilitation and Palliative Care Division, you will work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to deliver comprehensive, compassionate and patient-centred care to inpatients, outpatients and community-based consumers with complex and life-limiting illnesses.

In this role, you will contribute to the management and coordination of patient care, provide specialist consultation services, and support clinical decision-making across the service. You will play a key role in teaching and mentoring junior medical staff, medical students and other healthcare professionals, while also contributing to research, quality improvement initiatives and service development.

Working closely with colleagues across NALHN and community partners, you will help shape contemporary palliative care services that enhance quality of life, support patients and families, and uphold excellence in clinical practice. The role also offers opportunities to contribute to education, innovation and the ongoing development of palliative care services across the network and broader region.

To be eligible for this position, you must hold a Bachelor of Medicine; Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) or equivalent qualification and be eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia as a Medical Practitioner with Specialist Registration, or hold another qualification recognised under the South Australian Medical Officers Award.

The Total Indicative Remuneration figure is calculated taking into account base salary, leave loading and superannuation as well as managerial allowances, professional development or any other allowances where appropriate.

You are a dedicated and compassionate specialist in Palliative Care Medicine who is committed to delivering exceptional patient-centred care. You combine clinical excellence with strong leadership, communication and collaboration skills, enabling you to build effective relationships with patients, families and multidisciplinary teams. Passionate about education, quality improvement and service innovation, you are motivated to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people facing life-limiting illness while supporting the development of future healthcare professionals.

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows.
